transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um… I guess people have been noticing I’m kind of… slowed down sometimes. Like I take forever to answer or even get up from a chair. Other times I’m the opposite, just pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands a lot. It’s been noticeable enough that I figured I should come in.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have lost interest. I used to sketch, keep little notes about coffee I tried, go on weekend hikes… stuff like that. Lately I’ll open the notebook or put on my boots and it’s just… nothing. Like I don’t feel pulled to do it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um… it’s been a while. A little over two years, I think. Maybe around two years and a month. It lets up briefly sometimes, but it mostly comes back.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced these symptoms?
I think this is the main stretch. It’s been… about two years, maybe a little over, like two years and a month. There are short times where it eases up, but it hasn’t really gone away.
Have you had other periods in your life, before this current time, where you felt down or lost interest in things for a while?
Not really sure. I mean, I’ve had bad weeks before like anyone, but I don’t remember another stretch like this before.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so good that you didn’t feel like you needed sleep, or maybe even got into trouble because you were doing too much?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m a little more awake or busy, but not like… not needing sleep or getting into trouble from it.
Have you ever had a time before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
I don’t really think so. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, but I can’t say there was a two-week stretch like that before this.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
I don’t think so. I know I’ve already kind of said that, but… before this, I can’t really point to a time like that for two weeks straight.
Before this current period, was there ever a time when you felt down or lost interest in things so much that it affected your daily life, even if it didn’t last as long as it has now?
Not really. I mean, I’ve had bad days or been in a funk before, but I don’t think it was something that really messed up my day-to-day life like that.
Before this current period, was there ever a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a while, then felt better for at least a couple of months, and then this current period started?
I don’t think so. I can’t really remember a pattern like that—feeling bad for a while, then being okay for a couple months, and then this starting.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
No… not that I can think of. I know you asked before, but I really don’t remember anything like that before this.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things, then felt better for at least two months, and then eventually started feeling this way again?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t really remember having that kind of break and then it coming back before this.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, and then felt better for at least two months before this started again?
No… I don’t have a memory of that kind of thing happening before. Like, a long bad stretch and then a couple months okay before this… I don’t think so.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for a while, then felt better for at least two months, and then eventually started feeling this way again?
I don’t really know. I can’t think of a time like that before this, where it got better for months and then came back.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, which then went away completely for a while before this current period started?
I don’t think so. I can’t really remember anything like that before this… not where it fully went away for a while and then came back.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, which then went away completely for a while before this current period started?
I’m not really sure. I can’t point to a time before this where it was like that and then totally went away for a while.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, which then went away completely for a while before this current period started?
I mean… I don’t think so. I feel like I’ve already said it, but I can’t remember a clear stretch like that before this where it went away completely.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, and then felt completely better for at least two months before this current period started?
No… I don’t think I’ve had that. Not where I felt completely better for two months before this.

inference_history.note: The patient's presentation of slowed activity, loss of interest, and variability in behavior (at times slowed down, at times restless) is more consistent with depressive disorders. This rules out psychotic disorders (e.g., F20.x, F25.x) and bipolar disorders (F31.x) as the primary diagnosis at this point.

The chronic nature of the symptoms (lasting over two years) makes persistent depressive disorder (F33.2) a strong candidate. However, the presence of marked psychomotor retardation/ agitation and loss of interest supports major depressive disorder (F32.2) as still possible. The duration rules out F32.0 and F32.1 as the episode has lasted far beyond 2 weeks.

The patient reports a persistent low mood and loss of interest for over two years with only brief periods of relief, which supports the diagnosis of a recurrent depressive disorder (F33.2). However, since this episode has lasted more than two years and there is no clear history of prior episodes, it remains under consideration alongside a severe depressive episode (F32.2). No new disorders were ruled out this turn.
